title: JOIN NOWHERE EXPEDITIONS!
summary:
Have your neighbours already packed and moved to Endros? **Maybe it's time YOU do too!**

**Nowhere Expeditions** recruits specialists willing to relocate to Endros and participate in expeditions beyond the Gates. 
Vacancies for researchers, engineers, physicians, sailors, security personnel, salvagers, artificers, surveyors and many other roles.  

**Is it hard to describe your qualifications on official paperwork?** We can let you shine... In Endros!

**Scared of the remoteness?** Sell your lord! Sell your house! Bring your family! Bring your sheep! Bring your cow! You can build a whole new life in Endros!

Be scared not! In Endros, you'll start anew, working at the pinnacle of science and helping lead the world into a new era. The Era of Magic!
details:
# History
It has been 11 years since the [[why-we-call-them-the-valeoran-ruins|Valeoran Ruins]] were discovered by a University of Verna ship taking oceanographic measurements at the far ends of an uncharted horizon, far from any trade route, any shore and any explored land. Rising from the sea and reaching high into the sky, fragments of an ancient wonder remain suspended, drifting in place over an unnaturally still ocean. Today, floating platforms, laboratories, workshops, shipyards and habitation blocks surround the ruins, forming Endros: a rapidly growing settlement so remote that newspapers have taken the liberty of calling it "Endros in the Middle of Nowhere", "Endwhere" or just "Nowhere".

Several years after the initial discovery, researchers observed portions of the ruins beginning to move, gathering together and forming temporary portals known as *Gates*. What lies beyond them varies widely: Ruins, Unknown Ecosystems, Impossible machinery. Strange places where familiar rules no longer apply and resources found nowhere else in the known world. Materials recovered from Gates have created an entirely new field of technology known as *Artificery*. More recently, researchers have begun documenting something even stranger: *Magic*.

# Game Details
New to the campaign? Start with the **Onboarding** rules; each one ends with a link to the next, and the last, What's Next, explains when each **learning path** is worth reading. Pick those up when they matter to your character, or when they come up in play.

{{reading-path}}

You can also browse every rule by topic in the [Rules](game.html#rules) section, and the [Archive](archive.html) for more lore.

title: Nowhere Expeditions
summary: Nowhere Expeditions is a Fate campaign about **Expeditioners**: specialists who gather in Endros, form crews, and go through the Gates to bring back whatever they can find. This is the first Onboarding page: read them in order before your first expedition, each one ends with a link to the next.
details:
> **New here? Read the [game listing](game.html#post-game-listing) first.** It's the pitch for the campaign: how Endros came to be, what lies beyond the Gates and how the game runs. Then come back here and carry on.

### Endros and the Gates

Endros is the expedition hub. Every expedition starts and ends there. Gates open into impossible environments, and Expeditioners go through them for knowledge, materials, artifacts, money and answers.

Your character is an Expeditioner. You don't play the settlement, a guild or a fixed party. You play one person who decides which risks are worth taking.

### There is no permanent party

Each expedition has its own crew, made up of the players who sign up for it. You might travel with completely different people from one session to the next.

### You choose what to pursue

Opportunities appear on the [Job Board](jobs.html): Gates to survey, objects to recover, problems to solve. The players choose which ones to take on. None of them are mandatory, and none of them wait for a plot to catch up.

### The world is persistent

What one crew discovers, damages, opens, or leaves unfinished stays that way for the next crew. Reports go into the [Archive](archive.html), and changes to the settlement appear on the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html). A map drawn by one crew can save another crew's life.

### Play the way that suits you

There's no single right way to take part, and you don't need to attend every session. All of these are playing Nowhere Expeditions:

- joining expeditions through the Gates;
- working on Projects and Research between sessions;
- planning a Project with the GM and working out what it needs;
- roleplaying with other Expeditioners in Endros.

Do as much or as little of each as you enjoy. Each one changes the shared world in its own way.

### Between expeditions

Between expeditions your character has **Downtime**: time to work in Endros. Everything significant you do with it is a **Project Action**, whether you're building something, researching, recovering from an injury or repairing the settlement. The four-step Project Action is explained in [Downtime](game.html#post-downtime).

### You don't need to know the lore

You aren't expected to know the setting before you start. Knowledge is one of the main ways the campaign progresses: what the characters learn in play is a reward in itself. See *How Much Lore Should I Read?* in [Creating an Expeditioner](game.html#post-creating-an-expeditioner).

### Start here: Onboarding

These rules are all you need before your first expedition:

1. **Nowhere Expeditions** (this entry)
2. [Creating an Expeditioner](game.html#post-creating-an-expeditioner)
3. [Expeditions](game.html#post-expeditions)
4. [Downtime](game.html#post-downtime)
5. [Coins, Marketplace & Personal Stash](game.html#post-coins-marketplace-and-personal-stash)
6. [What's Next](game.html#post-whats-next)

Everything else is grouped into short **learning paths**, such as Between Expeditions, Gates & Discoveries or Spellcasting. [What's Next](game.html#post-whats-next) explains when each one is worth reading.

title: Creating an Expeditioner
summary: An Expeditioner is anyone with a reason to go through a Gate and a skill worth bringing. You don't need to be a fighter, and you don't need a long backstory: a clear idea of who you are, and why a crew would want you, is enough to start.
details:
### Start with three questions

- **Why are you in Endros?** Work, faith, debt, curiosity, exile, family, opportunity.
- **Why do you enter Gates?** What are you hoping to find, prove or escape?
- **Why would other Expeditioners want you in their crew?** This matters most in a campaign without a permanent party. Crews form around the skills a job needs.

Your answers become your **character concept**: one or two sentences that sum up who you are. For example, *"A disgraced harbor surveyor who maps Gates because nobody else will hire her"* or *"A field medic who keeps a ledger of every Expeditioner he couldn't save."*

### Specialists are encouraged

Characters don't need to be combat specialists. Cartographers, medics, linguists, riggers, cooks, mechanics and Gate scholars all earn their place on an expedition. Being excellent at one thing gives a crew a clear reason to invite you.

### Choose a Recruitment Faction

Most Expeditioners didn't simply appear in Endros on their own. A company, institution, government, employer, sponsor or personal arrangement usually helped them reach the Outpost and settle there.

Your **Recruitment Faction** represents that relationship.

- It grants a small **Extra**.
- It gives you its **Expedition Pack**: the kit you carry on every expedition.
- It may decide who your character knows, what they can access and what others expect of them.
- It does **not** decide your profession, your Skills or your role on an expedition.

Choose one from the [Recruitment Factions](game.html#path-recruitment-factions) learning path on the Rules tab. If none of them fit your character, you can be **Independent**. To see who the world's major powers are before you choose, browse the [Factions](factions.html) page. On your [character sheet](sheet.html), choose it as your **Sponsor**: you receive its Pack, and its Extra is written into your Extras for you.

### Your character sheet

Nowhere Expeditions uses Fate. The [character sheet](sheet.html) has a space for each of these. The detailed Fate rules explain how each one works in play.

- **Aspects** are short phrases that are true about your character, such as their concept, their trouble, a relationship or a belief. You invoke them for a bonus, and they can be compelled to complicate your life.
- **Skills** are what your character is good at, like Crafts, Lore, Notice or Physique, each with a rating. You roll them when the outcome is uncertain.
- **Stunts** are special tricks: narrow situations where your character gets a bonus or can do something unusual.
- **Stress and Consequences** show how much punishment your character can take. Stress is short-term and clears quickly. Consequences are lasting injuries or problems that need time and treatment. See [Consequences & Recovery](game.html#post-consequences-and-recovery).

### Equipment and your Personal Stash

Everything your character owns is kept in their **Personal Stash**. You buy equipment from the [Marketplace](marketplace.html) with **Coins**, and your Resources skill tops your Coins up after every expedition. You start with Coins equal to your Resources rating (none if it's +0 or lower), and with your Sponsor's **Expedition Pack**: it holds your basic supplies, and its **Carry Limit** decides how much extra Gear you can bring on an expedition. See [Coins, Marketplace & Personal Stash](game.html#post-coins-marketplace-and-personal-stash).

### Backstory

A few sentences are plenty. You don't need to know your character's whole history: things you discover in play can fill in the rest, and a blank space in your past can become a hook later.

### How Much Lore Should I Read?

Only read what your character would actually know. Pick the parts of the [Archive](archive.html) and the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html) that relate to your concept and leave the rest for later.

- **A religion-focused character:** read about the faiths and folklore your character follows. Other beliefs can stay strange to you.
- **An artificer or engineer:** look at the [Marketplace](marketplace.html), the Facilities on the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html), and [Resources](game.html#post-resources).
- **A Gate researcher:** read the Gate records in the Archive and the [Research](game.html#post-research) rules.
- **A spellcaster:** read [Spellcasting](game.html#post-spellcasting) and [Domains](game.html#post-domains).
- **A newly arrived outsider:** read almost nothing. Your character doesn't know how Endros works yet, and finding out is part of playing them.

Not knowing things can suit your character, and discovering the world through play is intended. The Archive will still be there when your character needs it.

title: Expeditions
summary: An expedition is one crew taking on one job beyond a Gate, and every expedition session follows the same three parts: **Preparation**, **Exploration** and **Return**.

title: Downtime
summary: Downtime is the time your character has between expeditions. Every significant piece of work in Endros, whether building, researching, crafting or recovering, is a **Project**, and you spend Downtime on **Project Actions** to move Projects forward.
details:
### Gaining Downtime

Each time an expedition is completed, Expeditioners gain Downtime:

| Your character… | Downtime gained |
| --- | --- |
| took part in the expedition | **2** |
| did not take part (stayed in Endros) | **3** |

Characters who stayed behind spent the whole expedition in Endros, so they have a little more time for work at home. Missing a session doesn't mean falling behind: you can still help the settlement and your character between expeditions.

**You can hold at most 8 Downtime.** Any Downtime you would gain above 8 is lost, so spend it rather than saving it up.

Your current Downtime is shown at the top of your character's page. The GM keeps it up to date.

### Every Downtime Action is a Project Action

Anything significant you do between expeditions is treated as a Project: a goal with a Progress track that fills up as people work on it. Building a device, studying an artifact, repairing the harbor and healing a wound all work the same way.

**The Project Action:**

1. **Spend 1 Downtime.**
2. **Describe what your character does** and which Skill they use.
3. **Roll** against a difficulty the GM sets for that approach.
4. **Gain Progress:**

| Result | Progress |
| --- | --- |
| Fail | 0, and a Complication |
| Tie | 1 |
| Success | 2 |
| Success with Style | 3 |

When every Progress box is filled, the Project is complete and its effect happens. Projects can be your own, shared with other characters or open to all of Endros. See [Projects](game.html#post-projects) for the full rules.

> **Example.** Mira wants to understand the humming shard her crew brought back. That's a Research Project. She spends 1 Downtime, studies the shard with **Lore**, succeeds, and marks 2 Progress.

### Two limits

- **One action per Project between expeditions.** Your character can make only one Project Action on any single Project between two expeditions. To finish a big Project faster, spread it over several expeditions or get other characters to work on it too. Each of them can also make one action on it.
- **Outpost help costs 1 extra Downtime.** If one of Endros's Capabilities genuinely helps your action, you may spend 1 more Downtime on that action to add the Capability's rating to the Progress you gain. This is still one action on the Project. See [Outpost Capabilities](game.html#post-outpost-capabilities).

### What doesn't cost Downtime

Casual roleplay, conversations, visiting other characters, buying gear at the Marketplace and small fictional actions are free. Downtime is only for significant work that has a mechanical effect.

### Why Downtime is limited

Downtime keeps between-session play fair. A player who is very active between sessions gets more stories and scenes, but not unlimited mechanical progress. Everyone's characters have about the same amount of time to work with.

### Recovering from Consequences

Injuries and other lasting harm, to you or to Endros, don't fade on their own. Each one is removed with a **Recovery Project**, using these same Project Actions. See [Consequences & Recovery](game.html#post-consequences-and-recovery).

title: Coins, Marketplace & Personal Stash
summary: Your character's equipment lives in their **Personal Stash**. You buy it at the Marketplace with **Coins**, your **Resources** skill tops your Coins up after every expedition, and your **Active Pack** decides how much extra Gear you can bring: its **Carry Limit**.
details:
### Coins

Your Coins are shown on your character's page and on your [character sheet](sheet.html).

- **Starting Coins:** a new Expeditioner starts with Coins equal to their Resources rating (none if it's +0 or lower).
- **Buying:** pay an item's [Marketplace](marketplace.html) price (its sale price, if it's discounted) and add it to your Personal Stash.
- Buying doesn't cost Downtime.
- **Availability:** an item's availability (Common, Restricted or Rare) doesn't change its price. Only items marked *Unavailable* can't be bought right now.
- **Rewards:** jobs and the GM can also give you Coins.

### Resources refreshes your Coins

After each expedition, every Expeditioner **refreshes** their Coins against their **Resources** skill:

- If you have **fewer** Coins than your Resources rating, raise them to that rating.
- If you have **as many or more**, keep what you have.
- If your character **took part** in the expedition, refresh first, **then** add any reward Coins.

A Resources rating of +0 or lower doesn't refresh anything.

> **Example.** Ines spent all her Coins and has Resources at Fair (+2). The next expedition ends, so she refreshes to **2**. Tomas also had 0 Coins and has Resources at Average (+1). He was on that expedition, which paid each crew member 3 Coins. He refreshes to 1, then adds the reward, for **4** Coins.

### Your Personal Stash

Your Personal Stash holds everything your character owns: what you bought, what Projects made for you (see [Personal Stash & Crafting](game.html#post-personal-stash-and-crafting)), what you were given, and your **Expedition Packs**. It's listed on your character's page.

### Expedition Packs

A **Pack** is your character's main carrying setup: a bag, frame or kit with a fixed list of ordinary supplies packed inside it, such as Rope, a Lantern and Rations.

- Your Personal Stash can hold several Packs, but only one is your **Active Pack** at a time.
- Your Active Pack sets your **Carry Limit**: how much additional Gear you can bring into action. Every starting Pack has a Carry Limit of **6**.
- What the Pack lists comes with it and **doesn't count** toward your Carry Limit. Neither does the Pack itself.
- A Pack holds exactly what it lists. If the list has no shovel, you have no shovel.
- Its contents are real things. Oil burns, Rations get eaten, Bandages get used, and a Rope tied across a chasm stays there. Mark what you use up, lose or leave behind on your character sheet. It stays gone until the GM restocks the Pack.

**Your Sponsor's Pack.** When you create your character, your Sponsor (your Recruitment Faction) gives you its Pack for free, and it becomes your Active Pack. Each Sponsor's rule shows what its Pack holds.

**Buying Packs.** Packs from your own Sponsor cost nothing. A Pack from another Sponsor costs **1 Coin**. They are listed under *Expedition Packs* in the [Marketplace](marketplace.html). You only ever need one of each: only one Pack is active at a time, so a second copy of the same Pack wouldn't help.

**Supplies and kits.** Small supplies such as a Ration, a Bandage or a flask of Lantern Oil are counted one by one inside your Pack, but they aren't sold one at a time. To bring more, take a **kit** from the Marketplace and bring it as additional Gear: a **Rations Kit** (weight 1) holds 5 Rations, a **Bandage Kit** (weight 1) holds 5 Bandages and a **Lantern Oil Kit** (weight 1) holds 3 flasks of Lantern Oil. Kits and ordinary basic Gear such as Rope, a Lantern or a Bedroll cost **0 Coins**. Each kit keeps its own count on your character sheet, beside your Pack's.

> **Example.** Your Pack holds 5 Rations. You add a Rations Kit (weight 1) to your additional Gear, so you have 10 Rations on the expedition, and only the kit counts toward your Carry Limit.

### Bringing Gear on an expedition

During Preparation (see [Expeditions](game.html#post-expeditions)):

1. Choose your **Active Pack**.
2. Check what is left inside it.
3. Mark the additional Gear from your Personal Stash that you're taking as **Brought into action**.

- The total weight of that additional Gear (each item's weight × how many you bring) can be at most your Active Pack's **Carry Limit**.
- Extra copies of something your Pack already holds count normally: if your Pack has one Rope and you bring a second one, the second Rope weighs 1.
- Without an Active Pack, no additional Gear fits.
- Some stunts let you carry more than your Pack allows, and some situations weigh you down. Note that as your **Carry modifier** on your character sheet (for example +1 or −1); it's added to your Active Pack's Carry Limit.
- Each item's weight and Tags are listed in the Marketplace. What Tags mean, and how Armor works: [Gear Tags & Armor](game.html#post-gear-tags-and-armor).

**Weight isn't how heavy something is.** It combines size, bulk, fragility, upkeep and how awkward the item is to keep at hand: how hard it is to bring with you. A sheet of paper can weigh more than a hammer if it has to stay perfectly dry.

> **Example.** Mira's Active Pack is the University Field Pack (Carry Limit 6), which already holds a Rope, a Lantern and Lantern Oil. She also brings a second Rope (weight 1) and a climbing kit (weight 3): 4 of her 6. The Rope inside her Pack doesn't count again. A second climbing kit would put her over the limit.

### Forgot something?

Gear you didn't bring isn't completely out of reach. During the expedition, you can declare that you had an item from your Personal Stash with you after all:

| If adding it would… | It costs |
| --- | --- |
| keep you **within** your Active Pack's Carry Limit | **1 stress**, on a stress track of your choice |
| take you **over** your Active Pack's Carry Limit | **1 Fate Point** |

Mark the item as brought into action. It stays with you for the rest of the expedition. You can only produce items you own: anything not in your Personal Stash is still back in Endros, or still in the Marketplace.

> **Example.** Halfway up a cliff, Mira realises she left a crowbar (weight 1) in her stash. She is carrying 4 of her 6, so she takes 1 stress and the crowbar was with her all along. Later she wants her second climbing kit too (weight 3, which would bring her to 8), so she spends a Fate Point.

### Keeping your sheet up to date

Use your [character sheet](sheet.html) for everything above:

- the **Coins** counter;
- your **Sponsor** and your **Expedition Pack**: which Pack is active, and what is left inside it;
- **Buy** buttons in its Marketplace tab, which take the price from your Coins (Packs at your price: free from your own Sponsor);
- **Brought into action** checkboxes, with your carried weight shown against your Active Pack's Carry Limit.

Press **Save file** and send the file to the GM, who brings the changes into the campaign records.

title: Gear Tags & Armor
summary: Gear has **Tags** such as `Cutting`, `Breaching` or `Loud` that say what it can do in the fiction; they give no numerical bonus. Some protective Gear has **Armor** boxes you mark instead of Physical Stress.
details:
### Gear Tags

Gear may have Tags such as `Cutting`, `Breaching`, `Loud`, `Magnetic` or `Breathing`. Tags describe what the equipment can do and how it behaves in the fiction.

Tags don't grant automatic numerical bonuses. A creature, hazard, environment or other rule may make a Tag important:

- A machete's `Clearing` Tag lets it cut through dense vegetation.
- A `Breaching` weapon suits a reinforced door.
- A `Loud` firearm may reveal your position.
- A `Magnetic` tool may interact unexpectedly with something found beyond a Gate.
- `Hearing Protection` may keep out a siren's song, and ordinary warnings too.

Choosing the right equipment is part of expedition preparation: learn something about a Gate, bring the Gear it calls for, and you have options the last crew didn't.

### Weapons

Weapons have no damage numbers. A weapon lets you act in the fiction, and its Tags say how. What it achieves depends on what you face: a creature's notes may say ordinary `Cutting` blades can't get through its shell, while a heavy `Blunt` blow can crack it.

Ordinary firearm ammunition isn't counted. Things whose limited supply matters, such as explosives, Flares, flamethrower fuel and breathing air, come in kits, and each kit keeps its own count on your [character sheet](sheet.html).

### Armor

Some protective Gear has **Armor boxes**.

> **Armor.** When you would take Physical Stress from something the Armor could reasonably protect you from, you may mark one Armor box instead. A marked Armor box can't be used again until the Armor is repaired or replaced.

- Armor only helps where physical protection makes sense. It doesn't protect against drowning, poison gas, sound, extreme heat, disease, or psychic or anomalous effects unless its Tags justify it.
- Like any other Gear, Armor only protects you if you brought it into action.
- Ordinary Armor has one or two boxes. Mark them on your character sheet.

> **Example.** A creature's claws would deal Nell 2 Physical Stress. She wears a Heavy Leather Coat (`Armor`, `Cutting`), so she marks its Armor box instead. The box stays marked until the coat is repaired.

title: What's Next
summary: You've read the essentials, and that's enough to make a character and join your first expedition. Everything else is in optional **learning paths**. Here's what each one covers, and when it's worth reading.
details:
### You don't need to read everything

The GM explains rules as they come up at the table, so nobody expects you to learn them all before you play. Learning paths are there for when you want to dig into something: because your character is about to do it, or because you're curious.

Each path is short, and its rules are meant to be read in order. Each rule ends with a link to the next.

### The learning paths

| Path | Read it when… |
| --- | --- |
| [Recruitment Factions](game.html#path-recruitment-factions) | **You're creating your character.** Pick the faction that brought them to Endros. |
| [Between Expeditions](game.html#path-between-expeditions) | **You're about to spend Downtime for the first time**, start a Project, research something, or your character has taken a Consequence. |
| [Gates & Discoveries](game.html#path-gates-discoveries) | **Your crew brings back something new**, or you want to understand Domains, Resources and their Functions. |
| [Crafting & Artificery](game.html#path-crafting-artificery) | **You want to build your own gear or invent a material.** Read Gates & Discoveries first. |
| [Spellcasting](game.html#path-spellcasting) | **Your character studies magic**, or a spell Form catches your eye. Read Resource Functions first. |
| [Building Endros](game.html#path-building-endros) | **You want to help the settlement grow** through Facilities, Capabilities or new Marketplace items. |

If you're not sure where to start, **Between Expeditions** is the one most players need soonest: almost everyone spends Downtime after their first expedition.

### Other ways to find things

- **Search:** press **Ctrl+K** (or the Search button) to search the whole site: rules, Gates, Resources, characters and more.
- **All rules:** pick *All rules* in the Topic menu to browse everything.
- **[Discoveries](discoveries.html):** everything expeditions have found so far, including Resources, Functions and spell Forms.
- **Ask:** the GM and the other players are happy to help, at the table or on Discord.

title: Nowhere Expeditions (the Company)
summary: **Nowhere Expeditions** is the name of this campaign, and also an in-world **company**: a recruitment and relocation agency that brings people from abroad to Endros and helps them settle in. Its recruits get the **Relocation Package**: +1 Coin after each expedition they take part in.

title: University of Verna
summary: The **University of Verna** is an academic institution with laboratories, archives and staff in Endros, and it sponsors scholars and field specialists to study the Gates. Its recruits get **Institutional Access**: +1 Progress on one Research Project Action between expeditions.

title: Independent
summary: **Independent** Expeditioners reached Endros on their own terms, without a major institution behind them. They owe nobody, and their own work comes first. **Self-Directed** gives them +1 Progress on one Personal Project Action between expeditions.

title: Vardic Holds
summary: The **Vardic Holds** are a loose federation of industrial northern jarldoms that send shipwrights, engineers and warriors to Endros. Their recruits get **Built to Endure**: once per session, a tied Crafts roll to fix or improvise equipment becomes a success with a free invoke.
details:
### Lore

The Vardic Holds are a loose federation of industrial northern jarldoms whose culture values craftsmanship, reputation, self-reliance and deeds worth remembering. They tend to see the Gates as another frontier to enter, understand and master.

The Holds back people who can build, fix and endure:

- shipwrights and engineers;
- smiths, riggers and other skilled workers;
- warriors;
- anyone whose work would carry a Vardic maker's mark with pride.

Their sponsorship comes as training, tools and practical support rather than paperwork.

A Recruitment Faction is who sponsored your character, not where they come from. You don't need to be Vardic to be sponsored by the Holds: your character may belong to the culture, come from somewhere else, disagree with its politics, or simply have been recruited by one of its institutions.

### Recruitment Extra

> **Built to Endure**
> Once per session, when you **Create an Advantage** using **Crafts** by repairing, reinforcing, modifying or improvising equipment, you may treat a **tie** as a **success with one free invoke** instead.

The benefit represents Vardic training, tools or practical sponsorship. It only changes a tie: a failure is still a failure.

> **Example.** The crew's winch jams halfway down a shaft. Sigrun rolls Crafts to rig it with spare chain and ties. With Built to Endure the repair holds properly: the crew gets the Aspect *Chain-Rigged Winch* with a free invoke.

### Expedition Pack

{{expedition-pack}}

### Expectations

The Holds may expect the people they back to:

- keep the oaths they swear;
- do work worthy of a maker's mark;
- uphold the reputation of whoever vouched for them;
- help other Vardic workers in Endros when asked.

These are hooks for roleplay, and possible Compels. They are not automatic penalties.

Choose your Recruitment Faction when you create your character (see [Creating an Expeditioner](game.html#post-creating-an-expeditioner)): pick it as your Sponsor on your character sheet: you receive its Pack, and its Extra is written into your Extras for you.

title: Aurelian Empire
summary: The **Aurelian Empire** is a powerful maritime empire of navy, bureaucracy and standardization. Its recruits get **Properly Provisioned**: once per session, bring one item from your Personal Stash into action for free.
details:
### Lore

The Aurelian Empire is a powerful maritime empire defined by its navy, its bureaucracy, standardization, etiquette and the belief that power creates responsibility. Aurelia treats magic as a strategic asset that needs responsible administration, and it wants capable people where that magic is found.

Imperial sponsorship is thorough. It comes with logistics, manifests, standardized supply and contingency plans, and it reaches:

- officers and administrators;
- engineers and technicians;
- specialists of every kind, properly equipped.

A Recruitment Faction is who sponsored your character, not where they come from. You don't need to be Aurelian to be sponsored by Aurelia: your character may belong to the culture, come from somewhere else, disagree with its politics, or simply have been recruited by one of its institutions.

### Recruitment Extra

> **Properly Provisioned**
> Once per session, bring one item from your Personal Stash into action **without paying** the normal Stress or Fate Point cost.

Normally, declaring mid-expedition that you had an item with you after all costs 1 stress, or a Fate Point if it takes you over your Active Pack's Carry Limit (see *Forgot something?* in [Coins, Marketplace & Personal Stash](game.html#post-coins-marketplace-and-personal-stash)). Properly Provisioned waives that cost once per session. The item still has to be in your Personal Stash, and once produced it counts as brought into action like any other.

> **Example.** Halfway up a cliff, Aldric realises his climbing kit is back in Endros. It isn't, of course: the manifest says it was packed. He marks it as brought into action and pays nothing.

### Expedition Pack

{{expedition-pack}}

### Expectations

Imperial sponsors may expect their people to:

- keep proper records, manifests and reports;
- maintain issued equipment to standard;
- conduct themselves with proper etiquette, especially before officials;
- report magical discoveries so they can be responsibly administered.

These are hooks for roleplay, and possible Compels. They are not automatic penalties.

Choose your Recruitment Faction when you create your character (see [Creating an Expeditioner](game.html#post-creating-an-expeditioner)): pick it as your Sponsor on your character sheet: you receive its Pack, and its Extra is written into your Extras for you.

title: Vesper Republic
summary: The **Vesper Republic** is a young revolutionary republic of citizenship, public argument and inquiry. Its recruits get **Someone Knows Someone**: once per session, a useful contact through the sponsor or one of its societies.
details:
### Lore

The Vesper Republic is a young revolutionary republic built around citizenship, public argument, inquiry and the belief that institutions must justify themselves. Vesper strongly resists monopolies over magical knowledge, and it would rather send its own people to the Gates than leave them to others.

Vesperian sponsorship usually comes through the Republic's affiliated societies, which open doors for:

- scientists, inventors and engineers;
- physicians and natural philosophers;
- citizens with a cause worth arguing for.

A Recruitment Faction is who sponsored your character, not where they come from. You don't need to be Vesperian to be sponsored by Vesper: your character may belong to the culture, come from somewhere else, disagree with its politics, or simply have been recruited by one of its institutions.

### Recruitment Extra

> **Someone Knows Someone**
> Once per session, establish that your Vesperian sponsor or one of its affiliated societies provided a **reasonable, useful contact** relevant to the problem.

The contact may provide information, an introduction or limited assistance. They may **not** solve the main problem, bypass a major obstacle, or know impossible secrets simply because you used this Extra. The GM decides who the contact is and what they can reasonably offer.

> **Example.** The crew needs to read the markings on a salvaged instrument. Odile uses Someone Knows Someone: a member of a society her sponsor works with has seen similar markings, and can tell the crew what kind of device it is. Working out how it functions is still up to them.

> **Working design.** This Extra may still change before the campaign starts.

### Expedition Pack

{{expedition-pack}}

### Expectations

Vesperian sponsors may expect their people to:

- share what they learn rather than hoard it;
- make their case openly when they disagree;
- return favours to the societies and contacts who help them;
- question institutions that can't justify themselves.

These are hooks for roleplay, and possible Compels. They are not automatic penalties.

Choose your Recruitment Faction when you create your character (see [Creating an Expeditioner](game.html#post-creating-an-expeditioner)): pick it as your Sponsor on your character sheet: you receive its Pack, and its Extra is written into your Extras for you.

title: Kharad Compact
summary: The **Kharad Compact** is a league of mercantile city-states, banks and merchant houses. Its recruits get **Established Credit**: an extra Mild Consequence slot, Minor Obligation, that covers a cost of up to 2 Coins now, paid back later with a finished Project.
details:
### Lore

The Kharad Compact is a league of mercantile city-states, banks, merchant houses and treaty networks whose civilization prizes agreement, reputation, patient negotiation and honest measure. Kharad sees the Gate era as a new world of value, risk, credit and exchange.

Kharadi sponsorship is a relationship with a merchant house, guild, bank, captain or intermediary that thinks your work will create value. They back:

- traders, agents and assessors;
- captains and crews;
- specialists whose finds could be worth something.

A Recruitment Faction is who sponsored your character, not where they come from. You don't need to be Kharadi to be sponsored by the Compact: your character may belong to the culture, come from somewhere else, disagree with its politics, or simply have been recruited by one of its institutions.

### Recruitment Extra

> **Established Credit**
> You have an extra **Mild Consequence slot**, called **Minor Obligation**. When you would pay **up to 2 Coins**, you can fill the slot instead: a merchant house, guild, bank, captain or intermediary covers the cost for you.

Write the debt, favour or contract in the slot, as an Aspect. The slot only ever holds obligations, never injuries, and while it's filled you can't use it again. You pay it back by **completing a Project and offering its result to the Kharad Compact**: the item, the finding or the finished work goes to your creditor instead of to you. Until then, the GM may let the obligation surface as a complication.

> **Example.** Yusra is 2 Coins short of a diving rig. A Kharadi chandler lets her take it on account, and she writes *Owes the Chandler a Favour* in her Minor Obligation slot. It stays there until she finishes a Personal Project, a set of Vaultvine climbing harnesses, and hands them to the chandler's house instead of keeping them.

> **Working design.** This Extra may still change before the campaign starts.

### Expedition Pack

{{expedition-pack}}

### Expectations

Kharadi sponsors may expect their people to:

- honour every agreement they make;
- deal in honest measure;
- settle their obligations, on time or by negotiation;
- protect their sponsor's reputation, and their own.

These are hooks for roleplay, and possible Compels. They are not automatic penalties.

Choose your Recruitment Faction when you create your character (see [Creating an Expeditioner](game.html#post-creating-an-expeditioner)): pick it as your Sponsor on your character sheet: you receive its Pack, and its Extra is written into your Extras for you.

title: Tianzhao Mandate
summary: The **Tianzhao Mandate** is an ancient bureaucratic civilization shaped by harmony, long-term consequence and celestial order. Its recruits get **Restorative Care**: +1 Progress on one Recovery Project Action between expeditions.
details:
### Lore

The Tianzhao Mandate is an ancient bureaucratic civilization whose politics and culture are shaped by harmony, long-term consequence, celestial order and a practical, administrative approach to the spirits it believes in. Tianzhao first read the Gates through its own ideas of the Spirit and Celestial realms, and it sends people to learn what they really are.

Its sponsorship comes with access to Tianzhao physicians, medicines, therapeutic traditions and spiritual care, and it supports:

- officials and scholars;
- physicians and engineers;
- specialists whose work touches the spirit world.

A Recruitment Faction is who sponsored your character, not where they come from. You don't need to be from Tianzhao to be sponsored by the Mandate: your character may belong to the culture, come from somewhere else, disagree with its politics, or simply have been recruited by one of its institutions.

### Recruitment Extra

> **Restorative Care**
> Once per between-expedition period, when you make progress on a **Recovery Project** for one of **your own** Consequences, gain **+1 additional Progress**.

Say how Tianzhao care helps: a physician's treatment, a medicine, a therapeutic practice, a rite. It applies only to Recovery Projects for your own Consequences (see [Consequences & Recovery](game.html#post-consequences-and-recovery)). A "between-expedition period" is the time between one expedition and the next.

> **Example.** Wen works on the Recovery Project *Set the Bone* for a broken leg, with the help of a Tianzhao physician's treatment. The Project Action succeeds for 2 Progress, and Restorative Care adds 1 more.

### Expedition Pack

{{expedition-pack}}

### Expectations

The Mandate may expect the people it sponsors to:

- weigh the long-term consequences of what they do;
- show proper respect to officials, ancestors and spirits;
- keep harmony within their crew;
- report what the Gates reveal about the Spirit and Celestial realms.

These are hooks for roleplay, and possible Compels. They are not automatic penalties.

Choose your Recruitment Faction when you create your character (see [Creating an Expeditioner](game.html#post-creating-an-expeditioner)): pick it as your Sponsor on your character sheet: you receive its Pack, and its Extra is written into your Extras for you.

title: Projects
summary: A Project is work too big to settle with a single roll, such as building a machine, repairing a district or understanding an artifact. Every kind of significant between-expedition work uses the same Project framework and advances one Project Action at a time.
details:
### What a Project contains

| Part | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Goal** | What the Project is trying to achieve. |
| **Type** | Personal, Public, Research and so on (see below). |
| **Progress** | How much work is needed, shown as boxes. The Project is complete when every box is filled. |
| **Requirements** | Things the Project needs in order to advance or finish. See [Project Requirements & Complications](game.html#post-project-requirements-and-complications). |
| **Relevant Outpost Capabilities** | The parts of Endros that can help. See [Outpost Capabilities](game.html#post-outpost-capabilities). |
| **Complications** | Problems that have come up along the way. |
| **Completion Effect** | What changes when the Project is complete. |

Projects appear on the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html) and in each character's Projects tab.

### Project Types

These are all the same system applied to different goals, not separate rules.

- **Personal Project:** your own work, usually for your character. See [Personal Stash & Crafting](game.html#post-personal-stash-and-crafting).
- **Public Project:** work for Endros that any character can contribute to.
- **Research Project:** answering a question. See [Research](game.html#post-research).
- **Marketplace Project:** making an item generally available. See [Marketplace Development](game.html#post-marketplace-development).
- **Facility Project:** adding a Facility to Endros. See [Facilities & Outpost Development](game.html#post-facilities-and-outpost-development).
- **Recovery / Repair Project:** fixing damage or a lasting problem. See [Consequences & Recovery](game.html#post-consequences-and-recovery).
- **Establish Supply Project:** making a Resource dependably available. See [Resources](game.html#post-resources).
- **Spell Innovation Project:** turning a combination of Words into a new Form. See [Spell Innovation](game.html#post-spell-innovation).

### The Project Action

Every Downtime Action is a Project Action (see [Downtime](game.html#post-downtime)). **Spend 1 Downtime**, then tell the GM:

1. what your character is doing;
2. which Skill they are using;
3. how that approach moves the Project forward.

The GM sets a difficulty based on how dangerous, uncertain or ambitious **that approach** is. Roll, and gain Progress:

| Result | Progress |
| --- | --- |
| **Fail** | 0, and a Complication is created |
| **Tie** | 1 |
| **Success** | 2 |
| **Success with Style** | 3 |

**Capability support:** if one of Endros's Capabilities genuinely helps with what you are doing, you may spend **1 extra Downtime** on the action to add that Capability's rating to the Progress gained. Only **one** Capability can support a single Project Action. See [Outpost Capabilities](game.html#post-outpost-capabilities).

**One action per Project between expeditions:** each character can make only one Project Action on a given Project between two expeditions. Spending extra Downtime for Capability support doesn't count as a second action.

> **Example.** Tomas works on *Restore the Harbor Crane*. He uses **Crafts** to rebuild the gearbox using the Workshops' tools, and spends 2 Downtime: 1 for the action and 1 so Endros's **Industry** supports it. The GM sets the difficulty at Fair (+2). Tomas succeeds: 2 Progress, plus Industry's rating. He can't work on the crane again until after the next expedition, but other characters can.

### Bigger Projects aren't harder to roll

A powerful Project shouldn't simply have a higher difficulty. Ambitious Projects instead need:

- more Progress;
- Requirements;
- several stages;
- specialized Facilities;
- recovered Resources;
- discoveries;
- expedition objectives.

### Project size (GM guidelines)

| Size | Progress |
| --- | --- |
| Minor | about 4 |
| Standard | about 6 |
| Major | about 10 |
| Grand | about 15 or more, or several stages |

These are guidelines for the GM. A Project can be bigger or smaller if the situation calls for it.

title: Project Requirements & Complications
summary: Two things can stop or change a Project: **Requirements**, which are things the Project needs, and **Complications**, which are new problems that come up while you work on it.
details:
### Requirement or Complication?

- **Requirement:** something the Project needs. It may be known from the start or found out while you work.
- **Complication:** a new problem caused by the work, usually after a failed or risky Project Action.

### Requirements

A Requirement is a known condition the Project needs. Common kinds:

| Requirement | Example |
| --- | --- |
| **Resource** | A Resource with the `Conduct` Function (see [Resource Functions](game.html#post-resource-functions)). |
| **Facility** | A containment lab to work safely. |
| **Knowledge** | Finished Research on how the artifact reacts to heat. |
| **Capability** | Endros's Medicine at a certain rating. |
| **Specialist / NPC** | A glassblower willing to work on Gate material. |
| **Previous Project** | The harbor must be repaired first. |
| **Expedition** | A sample has to be brought back from a specific Gate. |
| **Consequence slot** | Recovering a personal Severe Consequence needs a free Moderate slot (see [Consequences & Recovery](game.html#post-consequences-and-recovery)). |

If a Requirement is missing, the Project may be **Paused**. You can't advance it until that need is met. A Paused Project keeps its Progress.

### Complications

Complications should create new problems to deal with, not simply wipe out Progress. A Complication might be:

- a new **Aspect** attached to the Project, such as *Unstable Prototype* or *The Foreman Has Doubts*;
- a problem that makes future Project Actions harder;
- a **Blocking Complication** that pauses the Project until it is resolved;
- extra Progress needed;
- a new material or knowledge Requirement;
- an **expedition objective**.

> **Example.** A failed Project Action on *Calibrate the Resonance Lens* cracks the only lens. The GM adds a Complication: *Replacement lens glass must be recovered from the Gate where the original was found.* That becomes a new listing on the Job Board.

Complications that lead to expeditions are especially valuable. They send work from the Settlement Loop back into the Expedition Loop and give crews a reason to go somewhere.

When a Complication is resolved, the Project records how it was dealt with.

title: Research
summary: Research is a Project whose goal is an answer. It uses the same Downtime, Project Action and Progress rules as every other Project and doesn't have a separate system.

title: Consequences & Recovery
summary: Consequences are lasting harm, to your character or to Endros. In this campaign they don't fade with time: you work them off with **Recovery Projects**, and each finished Recovery Project makes the Consequence one step less severe.
details:
### This replaces Fate's recovery rules

In standard Fate, a Consequence clears after enough time passes once recovery starts. **Nowhere Expeditions doesn't use that rule.** A Consequence, whether personal or on the Outpost, stays until a Recovery Project lowers it.

### Severity sets the Progress

A Recovery Project needs as much Progress as the Consequence's severity:

| Personal Consequence | Outpost Consequence | Progress needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mild | Low | 2 |
| Moderate | Moderate | 4 |
| Severe | High | 6 |
| — | Critical | 8 |

### Each Recovery Project lowers it one step

Completing a Recovery Project doesn't remove the Consequence outright. It brings it down **one tier**:

- Severe becomes Moderate, Moderate becomes Mild, and a Mild Consequence is removed.
- On the Outpost, Critical becomes High, High becomes Moderate, Moderate becomes Low, and a Low Consequence is removed.

Rewrite the Consequence to fit its new severity and move it into that slot. Then start a new Recovery Project for the next step if you want to keep going.

### The lower slot must be free

A personal Consequence can only step down into an **empty** slot, so each personal Recovery Project has a Requirement (see [Project Requirements & Complications](game.html#post-project-requirements-and-complications)):

| Recovering a… | Requires a free… |
| --- | --- |
| Severe Consequence | Moderate slot |
| Moderate Consequence | Mild slot |
| Mild Consequence | nothing; it is simply removed |

If the slot below is taken, the Recovery Project is **Paused** until it is free. Usually that means recovering the lighter Consequence first.

This applies only to personal Consequences. The Outpost has no slot limits, so its Consequences can always step down.

> **Example.** Tomas comes back from a Gate with the Severe Consequence ***Shattered Leg*** and the Moderate Consequence ***Cracked Ribs***. His Moderate slot is taken, so the leg has to wait.
>
> 1. **Strap the Ribs** (4 Progress, needs his Mild slot free, which it is). The ribs become Mild: ***Sore Ribs***. His Moderate slot is now free.
> 2. **Set the Bone** (6 Progress). The leg becomes Moderate: ***Leg in a Splint***.
> 3. **Rest the Ribs** (2 Progress). ***Sore Ribs*** is removed, which frees his Mild slot.
> 4. **Learn to Walk on It Again** (4 Progress). The leg becomes Mild: ***Stiff Knee***.
> 5. **Back to Full Strength** (2 Progress). The last Consequence is gone.

### Working on a Recovery Project

Recovery uses the normal Project Action (see [Downtime](game.html#post-downtime) and [Projects](game.html#post-projects)), including the one-action-per-Project limit between expeditions.

- **The approach has to make sense.** A broken leg needs setting and rest, and a shaken mind needs help or resolution. The GM may require a suitable Facility, an NPC healer or particular circumstances.
- **Others can help.** A crewmate who is a field medic can spend their own Downtime on your Recovery Project. Each character can still make only one action on it between expeditions.
- **Medicine** (for people) or another fitting Capability (for the Outpost) can support an action for 1 extra Downtime. See [Outpost Capabilities](game.html#post-outpost-capabilities).

### Outpost Consequences

When Endros's stress track is full, the settlement takes a Consequence, recorded on the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html). Its Recovery Project is a **Public Project**: anyone can work on it.

> **Example.** Endros takes the High Consequence ***Industrial District Damaged***.
>
> **Repair the Industrial District**: Public Recovery Project, 6 Progress, supported by Industry or Infrastructure. When it's complete, the Consequence drops to Moderate, for example ***Industrial District Running at Half Capacity***.

### Consequences are opportunities too

An Outpost Consequence should be more than a penalty. A damaged district means displaced workers, missing supplies, salvage opportunities and maybe someone who caused it. All of these are things to investigate, fix or take advantage of.

title: Domains
summary: Every Gate has a **Domain**: the broad kind of environment it is, such as Volcanic or Frozen. Its Resources, creatures and hazards inherit that Domain, so a Stunt, a piece of equipment or a specialism can be built around one.

title: Resources
summary: A **Resource** is a catalogued material: usually something recovered from a Gate, such as a material, organism, substance or component, and sometimes an ordinary trade good from the wider world. Whoever discovers one **names it**. Its **Functions** say what it can do, and its **Availability** says how much of it Endros can use.
details:
Every Resource found so far is listed in [Discoveries](discoveries.html#resources).

### Specimens

Expeditioners can recover almost anything they can safely carry out of a Gate.

Until it has been studied, an unfamiliar material or object is simply a **Specimen**. A Specimen does not need to possess a Function and is not automatically a Resource.

Expeditioners might return with plants, stone, soil, water, biological remains, strange residues, fragments of structures, manufactured objects or anything else they believe may be worth examining.

Research may determine that a Specimen is:

- ordinary or currently of no practical use;
- scientifically interesting but not exploitable;
- an Artifact requiring separate study;
- or a **Resource** with one or more useful Functions.

Once a useful anomalous property has been identified, the discovery is entered into the Resource catalogue. Whoever makes the discovery may name the new Resource.

Materials previously considered unimportant can be studied again if later discoveries provide new reasons to investigate them.

### What a Resource has

| | | Example: Emberglass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Name** | Chosen by whoever discovered it. | Emberglass |
| **Description** | What it looks and feels like. Fiction, not mechanics. | Glassy shards that soak up heat and stay warm for days. |
| **Domain** | The kind of Gate it came from (see [Domains](game.html#post-domains)), or for an ordinary trade good, the culture it comes from. | Volcanic |
| **Functions** | What it can do (see [Resource Functions](game.html#post-resource-functions)). | `Store`, `Heat` |
| **Special Property** | Odd behavior too specific to be a Function. | Rings faintly when two shards touch. |
| **Availability** | How much of it Endros has. | Limited |

> **Descriptions make Resources memorable. Functions make them useful. Special Properties make them strange.**

### You name what you discover

When Expeditioners bring back something nobody has recorded before, **they name it**. If a whole crew found it, the crew agrees on the name. From then on, everyone in Endros calls it that.

### Hidden Functions

Some Functions are understood as soon as a Resource is recovered. Others are **Hidden**: they're already in the material, but nobody understands them yet. [Research](game.html#post-research) can reveal them, so a Resource brought back long ago can suddenly become valuable.

### Availability

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Sample** | A handful of specimens. Enough for Research, not for production. |
| **Limited** | A real stock, but using it uses it up. Enough for a prototype or a single Project. |
| **Available** | A dependable supply. Routine Projects don't need to count it. |

A Resource becomes **unavailable** if its supply runs out or its source is lost.

### Establishing a supply

To make a Resource more available, start a Public Project: **Establish [Resource] Supply** (see [Projects](game.html#post-projects)). That might mean surveying deposits, working out extraction or storage, building infrastructure, arranging transport or securing access.

- If the source is an open Gate, **access to that Gate** may be a Requirement. If the Gate closes, the Project is **Paused**, and its Progress is kept.
- Once a source is lost, an Available Resource slowly becomes Limited as stockpiles run down.
- Cultivation, domestication, manufacture, synthetic substitutes and [Material Engineering](game.html#post-material-engineering) can also provide a supply.

Once a supply is established, it stays established. Nobody replays routine harvesting trips.

title: Resource Functions
summary: **Functions** are the shared vocabulary of artificery and magic. Each one is a verb describing what a Resource can **do**, such as `Store`, `Heat` or `Move`. Projects ask for Functions, Spellcasting manifests them as Words, and how two Functions interact tells you whether combining them is easy, hard or dangerous.
details:
Look up any Function, combine them and see their interactions in the [Functions explorer](discoveries.html#functions).

### Capabilities, not appearance

A Function is an exceptional, exploitable property, not a description.

- A crystal isn't automatically `Glow`, and a heavy material isn't automatically `Anchor`.
- **Ordinary materials have no known Functions.** Ordinary steel is durable, but that doesn't make it a `Reinforce` Resource.
- Behavior too specific to be a Function is a Special Property (see [Resources](game.html#post-resources)).

### The vocabulary

The GM keeps this list. A Function exists only once the GM adds it, and new ones may appear as the campaign discovers them.

{{function-vocabulary}}

### Functions combine

Instead of a new Function for every effect, effects are combinations:

| Effect | Written as |
| --- | --- |
| Burning, giving off heat | `Release` + `Heat` |
| Cooling, freezing | `Absorb` + `Heat` |
| Propulsion | `Move` + `Release` |
| Stopping motion | `Absorb` + `Move` |
| Explosive discharge | `Store` + `Release`, perhaps with `Amplify` |

The same combinations describe magic: Spellcasting combines Words into Forms (see [Spellcasting](game.html#post-spellcasting)).

### How Functions interact

| Kind | Example | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Synergy** | `Store` + `Release` | They support each other. Comparatively easy to engineer. It doesn't give extra Progress. |
| **Opposition** | `Conduct` + `Dampen` | They work against each other. Still possible, with clever design, extra Resources, Research, a Facility or a harder Project. |
| **Instability** | `Catalyze` + `Release` | Dangerous or unpredictable together. Not forbidden, and often the most valuable frontier. |

An interaction can carry a **keyword** naming the specific effect, such as *Runaway*, *Overload* or *Cancellation*. A pair can have more than one kind: `Store` and `Release` work well together, but discharge catastrophically if uncontrolled.

For a difficult combination, the GM may raise the difficulty, add Requirements (a Catalyst, a Facility, Research), split the work into stages or make failures harsher. **Interactions are guidance, not a chemistry table.** The GM decides how a particular combination behaves.

### How many Functions?

Most Resources have **one to three**. One is a fairly simple Resource, two is a typical interesting one, three is unusually valuable, and four or more is exceptional.

### Reading a Requirement

Projects ask for Functions, not named materials (see [Project Requirements & Complications](game.html#post-project-requirements-and-complications)):

> **Material Requirement:** a Resource with `Store` and `Conduct`.
>
> Requires `Stabilize` and either `Dampen` or `Nullify`.

Any known Resource with the Functions will do. When you offer one, explain how it solves the engineering problem.

title: Material Engineering
summary: When no known Resource has the Functions a Project needs, an artificer, engineer or researcher can try to **make one**. Material Engineering is optional advanced play for characters who enjoy invention.

title: Personal Stash & Crafting
summary: A Personal Project can create, modify or restore an item for your character. When it is finished, the item goes into your **Personal Stash**, but making one working item doesn't make it available to everyone in Endros.
details:
### Making an item

Use a Personal Project (see [Projects](game.html#post-projects)) to:

- **create** a new item;
- **modify** an item you already have;
- **restore** a damaged item or an artifact.

The Project's Requirements often include Resources with particular Functions (see [Resource Functions](game.html#post-resource-functions)). When the Project is complete, the item is added to your **Personal Stash**, and it counts toward your Active Pack's Carry Limit like any other Gear when you bring it into action (see [Coins, Marketplace & Personal Stash](game.html#post-coins-marketplace-and-personal-stash)).

### One item is not a product line

Creating a working item gives **you** that item. It doesn't mean Endros can make more.

> **Example.** Ines finishes a Personal Project and creates **Gate-Silk Armor**. She owns the prototype and can wear it on her next expedition. Nobody else can buy Gate-Silk Armor yet.
>
> If the crews want it to become generally available, someone needs to start a **Marketplace Project**, and Ines's prototype might be one of its Requirements.

### Summary

| Project | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **Personal Project** | One item, in your Personal Stash. |
| **Marketplace Project** | The item can be bought by everyone. See [Marketplace Development](game.html#post-marketplace-development). |

title: Spellcasting
summary: Magic uses the same vocabulary as artificery. **Artificery studies Functions embodied in matter; Spellcasting manifests those same Functions directly as magical Words.** A caster manifests Words and uses learned **Forms** to turn them into repeatable effects.
details:
### Where magic comes from

Magic only became possible once Gate artifacts and phenomena let researchers begin to understand the Functions underneath them. Spellcasting is an emerging experimental science, not an ancient, complete spell list.

The whole system is one chain:

1. Gates contain environments, and environments produce Resources.
2. Resources embody Functions, and Research reveals them.
3. Artificery combines Functions through matter.
4. Spellcasting manifests Functions as **Words**.
5. **Forms** combine Words into repeatable magical effects.
6. Projects turn discoveries into permanent additions to Endros.

### Words

A **Word** is one Resource Function manifested as magic, such as `Heat`, `Move`, `Anchor`, `Record` or `Phase`. The vocabulary is the same as in [Resource Functions](game.html#post-resource-functions).

- A caster may know how to manifest some Words and not others.
- **Knowing a Word doesn't grant every use of it.** Specific effects need learned Forms.
- A manifested Word has temporary **Stress capacity**: how much magical potential is left in it.

### Basic Forms

A **Basic Form** is the learned technique for manifesting one Word. *Basic Form: Heat* lets you manifest `Heat`. A caster who hasn't learned the Basic Form for `Phase` can't normally manifest `Phase` themselves.

**You can skip the Basic Form** when the Word, or the matching Function, is already within reach:

- a Word that is already manifested;
- a prepared magical object;
- a Resource with that Function;
- an effect in the environment or scene;
- another caster's manifestation, where that makes sense.

Access isn't unlimited capacity. Something being within reach doesn't make it an endless supply.

### Forms and Spells

A **Form** is a learned technique that uses one or more Words to create a specific, repeatable effect. Every Form is learned separately: knowing the Words a Form uses doesn't mean you know the Form.

| Tier | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Basic Form** | Manifests one Word. |
| **First Form** | Uses one Word to produce a defined effect. |
| **Second Form** | Combines two Words for a more complex effect. |
| **Third Form** | Combines three Words for an advanced effect. |

Some examples of how Words compose (not a finished spell list):

| Form | Words | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kindle | `Heat` | Raise a target's temperature. |
| Kinetic Impulse | `Move` | Alter a target's motion. |
| Flash Freeze | `Absorb` + `Heat` | Draw the heat out of a target. |
| Thermal Burst | `Release` + `Heat` | A sudden release of thermal energy. |
| Kinetic Arrest | `Absorb` + `Move` | Remove or reduce motion. |
| Dimensional Lock | `Anchor` + `Phase` | Prevent or interfere with spatial displacement. |
| Gate Signature Reading | `Sense` + `Resonate` | Detect a relevant Gate signature. |

### Where a Word is manifested

| Host | Capacity | Control | Main risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Self** | your own | high | It uses up your own Stress capacity, and failures or overload hit you directly. |
| **Object** | limited | high | The object can be lost, damaged, stolen or disrupted. |
| **Scene** | large | low | Others, including enemies, can use it, and it can react with Resources or other Words nearby. |

- **Self:** the Word manifests through you. It's the fastest, most portable and most controlled method, and the hardest for anyone else to tap. It's also the personally risky one.
- **Object:** the Word is manifested into a wand, weapon, staff, crystal, ring, prepared focus or artificed device. It doesn't use your own Stress and can be prepared ahead of time, but its capacity is limited. Resources and crafting can make an object better at hosting particular Words.
- **Scene:** the Word is manifested into the environment itself. That gives large capacity, suited to rituals and powerful Forms, and several casters may draw on it. But it's hard to control, and dangerous Function combinations in the scene can cause Complications. A scene manifestation can act as both a Stress pool and a Scene Aspect.

### Word Stress

Words use **Stress** as magical capacity. Forms may consume Stress from the Words they use. A Word stays available while it has usable capacity. When its Stress runs out, the manifestation dissipates, goes inert or otherwise stops providing capacity.

### Resources and spellcasting

A Resource with a Function can give a caster **access** to the matching Word. For example, Emberglass (`Store`, `Heat`) can open the way to Heat-related techniques.

But **a physical Function is not an unlimited manifested Word.** Functions provide access or potential; Words provide magical capacity. Carrying one Resource with several Functions isn't the same as having several permanent Words.

> **Still being designed:**
> - Word Stress values and track lengths;
> - manifestation difficulties and the Skills used;
> - the Stress each Form costs;
> - how many Words can be manifested at once;
> - how capacity is drawn directly from Resources;
> - how Words and Forms are learned, and what that costs.
>
> Until these are set, the GM rules case by case.

### Known Forms

The Forms Endros has recorded (also in [Discoveries](discoveries.html#forms), alongside the Words they use):

{{form-list}}

New Forms come from research and experiment; see [Spell Innovation](game.html#post-spell-innovation).

title: Spell Innovation
summary: There's no universal spell list to learn from. New **Forms** are invented, and a **Spell Innovation Project** turns a theoretical combination of Words into a reliable, repeatable technique.

title: Outpost Capabilities
summary: Capabilities describe what Endros can reliably support as a settlement. Each has a rating on the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html), and a Capability can add Progress when the settlement's people, tools or expertise genuinely help your Project.
details:
### The six Capabilities

| Capability | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| **Industry** | Crafting, repairs and manufacturing. |
| **Research** | Investigation, analysis and Gate knowledge. |
| **Commerce** | Trade, funding and access to resources. |
| **Security** | Defense, policing and emergency response. |
| **Medicine** | Treatment and recovery. |
| **Infrastructure** | Facilities, transportation and services. |

The Outpost Sheet also lists the Facilities and characters behind each Capability: the workshops, laboratories and docks that do the work.

### Capabilities in Project Actions

When you make a Project Action (see [Projects](game.html#post-projects)), you may **spend 1 extra Downtime** to have one relevant Capability **add its rating to the Progress you gain**, as long as the settlement is actually helping you.

- Rebuilding an engine in the Workshops: **Industry** helps.
- Rebuilding it alone in a tent at the edge of a Gate: Industry probably doesn't help.

A Capability isn't an automatic solution. You still describe what your character is doing and roll a Skill. The Capability adds to the result. Only one Capability can support each Project Action, and the extra Downtime doesn't count as a second action on the Project.

> **Example.** Mira studies a preserved Gate organism in the University laboratories. She spends 2 Downtime: 1 for the action and 1 for the laboratory's help. She rolls Lore and succeeds for 2 Progress, then adds Endros's Research rating because the laboratory's equipment and staff are part of her approach.

### Capabilities as Requirements

Advanced Projects may need a Capability at a certain rating before they can start or finish. For example, a surgical procedure on a Gate-touched patient might need a certain level of Medicine. See [Project Requirements & Complications](game.html#post-project-requirements-and-complications).

### Improving Capabilities

Capabilities can change over time. Facilities and completed Projects can improve them, and Outpost Consequences can strain them. See [Facilities & Outpost Development](game.html#post-facilities-and-outpost-development).

title: Facilities & Outpost Development
summary: A Facility is a permanent addition to Endros, such as a laboratory, hospital wing or workshop, and it is usually built through a **Public Project** that many characters work on across many expeditions.
details:
### How a Facility gets built

1. **Someone proposes it** and explains what it is for.
2. **The GM defines its Completion Effect**: what Endros can do once it exists.
3. **Requirements are set** (see [Project Requirements & Complications](game.html#post-project-requirements-and-complications)).
4. **Players spend Downtime** on Project Actions (see [Projects](game.html#post-projects)).
5. **Missing Requirements** may lead to Research or expedition objectives.
6. **When the Project is complete**, the Facility joins Endros and appears on the [Outpost Sheet](outpost.html).

### What Facilities do

Facilities should mostly create **new possibilities** rather than just add numbers. A Facility might:

- unlock new kinds of Project;
- allow safe work with dangerous materials;
- meet Requirements for other Projects;
- unlock new Marketplace items;
- offer special Preparation actions before expeditions;
- make recovery possible for certain Consequences;
- improve or expand an Outpost Capability (see [Outpost Capabilities](game.html#post-outpost-capabilities));
- allow Research that was impossible before.

> **Example: a Containment Laboratory.**
> - **Proposed because:** nobody can safely study Resources that combine `Catalyze` and `Release`. Two samples have already exploded in the University.
> - **Type:** Public Project (Facility), Major, about 10 Progress
> - **Requirements:** Research at a set rating; a shielding material with `Stabilize` and either `Dampen` or `Nullify`; a qualified overseer
> - **Completion Effect:** Projects that handle unstable Resources can be worked on safely in Endros, and it adds a Research Capability asset.

### A shared achievement

Because a Public Project is open to everyone, a Facility is usually built by many players over several expeditions. One character proposes it, another crew brings back the shielding, and someone who has missed three sessions spends their extra Downtime finishing it. Whoever completes it, the result is part of Endros for every crew that follows.

title: Marketplace Development
summary: A **Marketplace Project** is Endros learning to reliably make, acquire or distribute an item. When it is finished, the item appears in the [Marketplace](marketplace.html) and any Expeditioner can get it there.
